subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If x = a cos³t and y = a sin³t, find dy/dx.

mark_split.label: Differentiate x and y with respect to t

The answer −tan t was checked numerically before it was written: with a = 2 and t = 0.7 the difference quotient (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) reads −0.8422883805 against −tan(0.7) = −0.8422883805; with a = 5 and t = 1.1 it reads −1.964759657 against −1.964759657; with a = 3 and t = −0.4 it reads 0.4227932188 against 0.4227932187. recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you differentiate with respect to first, and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate x and y with respect to t
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the parametric rule before differentiating anything. The chain rule is used once in each line — differentiate the cube first, then multiply by the derivative of the trigonometric function inside it.
steps.memory_tip: Both derivatives read the same way: 3a, the square of the same function, then the derivative of that function. Only cos t brings a minus sign with it.
lines: x and y are both given in terms of t,
x = a cos³t  ⇒  dx/dt = 3a cos²t · (−sin t) = −3a cos²t sin t

lines.text: y\ = \ a\sin ^{3} t\ \Rightarrow \ \dfrac{dy}{dt}\ = \ 3a\sin ^{2} t\ \cdot \ \left(\cos t\right)\ = \ 3a\sin ^{2} t\cos t

recall.must_convey: That dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt), with dx/dt = −3a cos²t sin t and dy/dt = 3a sin²t cos t.
accept: differentiate both x and y with respect to t first
use the parametric rule d y by d t over d x by d t
d x by d t is minus three a cos squared t sin t
rendintini t tho differentiate cheyyali, tarvata divide cheyyali
d y by d t is three a sin squared t cos t
heard_as: three a cos squared t sin t

steps.why: There is no equation linking x and y directly, so neither can be differentiated with respect to the other. x and y are connected through the parameter t, so both are differentiated with respect to t first.
common_mistakes: Writing dx/dt as 3a cos²t, which leaves out the derivative of cos t inside.
Dropping the minus sign that comes from differentiating cos t.

steps.label: Divide to get dy/dx
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the fraction out before cancelling — the mark is for the division, not for the two words −tan t on their own.
steps.memory_tip: After cancelling, −sin t over cos t is left, so the answer is −tan t.
lines: The factor 3a cancels, and one sin t
and one cos t cancel as well.

lines.text: (sin²t/sin t = sin t and cos t/cos²t = 1/cos t;
this needs sin t ≠ 0 and cos t ≠ 0)

recall.must_convey: That dividing dy/dt by dx/dt cancels 3a, sin t and cos t and leaves −tan t.
accept: divide d y by d t by d x by d t
the three a cancels and it becomes minus tan t
sin t over cos t with a minus sign
a cancel aipothundi, answer minus tan t
the answer is minus tan t

steps.why: Every a cancels, so the answer depends only on t and not on the size of the curve.
common_mistakes: Dividing dx/dt by dy/dt instead, which gives −cot t.
Leaving a in the final answer, when every a has already cancelled.
lines_compact: The factor 3a cancels, and one sin t
and one cos t cancel as well.

insider_note: Both are given through t, so use dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) ; there is no need to eliminate t. The 3a and one factor each of sin and cos cancel, leaving −tan t.
